name: Cell Project Space
summary: An artist-founded gallery on Cambridge Heath Road, started in 1999 and at its current Bethnal Green site since 2003. A ground-floor event space was added in the summer of 2019.

accessibility.notes: Level access to the entrance through a courtyard gate; ring to be let in. The gallery is on the first floor, with a wheelchair lift and staff to help. Shallow ramps lead into the ground-floor event space. The nearest accessible toilet is about 100 metres away at the Museum of Childhood.

story.opened: 1999, as 12 artists' studios with a small project space, in a former furniture factory in Dalston
story.then: The venue's own website says Cell left that Tyssen Street building in 2001 when the site was redeveloped and moved to Ideal House on Arcola Street, a former textiles factory, before settling on Cambridge Heath Road in 2003. In 2011 it began Cyclorama, a run of commissioned solo shows lasting a year each. Its Cycle Club events ended in 2013. A ground-floor event space opened in summer 2019, and the Cellular platform and residency programme was launched.
story.now: According to the venue's own website, the gallery opens Thursday to Sunday, 12 to 6pm, and the office is staffed Monday to Friday. Besides the first-floor gallery, the ground floor holds a reading room and an events room. Cell Studios, which funds the gallery, operates six sites across East London.
worth_knowing: The venue's own website says Cell has worked with over 300 artists.
The venue's own website says Cell built and looks after a public green space next to the site on Cambridge Heath Road.
It began in a run-down Victorian furniture factory on Tyssen Street, Dalston, according to the venue's own website.
